🟡 [k6-r2-r3-verbatim-claims-false] MUST-FIX The disposition rows tagged R2 and R3 claim "relocated verbatim", but that claim cannot be true. hooks/tests/profile-guided-dispositions.test.sh:101-102 (dead-disposition case) shows the guided check rejects any disposition whose hash is still present in the inventory sources. So every accepted R2 row whose target is skills/dev-flow/SKILL.md or skills/ceo-agent/SKILL.md (both ARE the two inventory files, despite the text "outside the two-file rule inventory") is, by construction, not present verbatim. The diff confirms this. P0 "git rev-parse HEAD > .claude/session-start-sha" now exists only as the inline "`mkdir -p .claude && git rev-parse HEAD > …`" (skills/dev-flow/SKILL.md:~129, intent gate 1). "git branch --show-current", "1. `git checkout -b hotfix/<description> main`", "**Backlog safety** (before deferring anything):", "Deploy per project config (default: build + restart)." and "> rollback is verified stable." survive only as reworded table cells or wrapped prose. R3's "3. Skill routing check for the target code area." is now "5. Skill routing check…" in skills/dev-flow/references/context-continuation.md:~27. Impact: the 3.0.0 audit record that the owner asked to be honest misstates how 9+ removed baseline lines were handled. A future auditor trusting R2/R3 would believe the text is preserved byte-for-byte when it was restated. Smallest fix: re-tag those R2/R3 rows (f56a42069910, 5079ab293bb2, 09e1b8ad839c, 234b38b50622, e5cce84ef9e9, 996eb540a14e, 1a0387f70733, c67a728b91f9, dc15c2f45b5b, 4f9a46a6f307, b8eaad6ea295) to the R1 "dropped or restated" rationale, then regenerate and re-pin profiles. Dev-flow 555 → finish-flow should be checked the same way. Obligations themselves are carried (intent gates 1–2, start-gate branch check, verify backlog safety, Staging Gate, Urgent section, context-continuation step 5), so no requirement is lost.
🔵 [k6-inventory-bound-slack] CUT/FOLLOW-UP At hooks/tests/profile-context-isolation.test.sh:205-210, `canonical_rules + dispositionCount >= baseline` sums all 405 dispositions, including the 41 pre-range ones and any `rewritten` ones, against a real shortfall of 815-689=126. That leaves about 279 rules of slack, so this inequality alone would not catch an unaccounted removal. It is not vacuous in aggregate because the exact `"canonical_rules": 689` pin (:284) and the guided compatibility check enforce the exact relation. A tighter bound would count only dispositions whose hash is absent from the current extraction. Excluded because the redundant exact checks already fail closed.
🔵 [k6-urgent-probe-xs-s] CUT/FOLLOW-UP The "Leaving the last verify of an urgent session" row (skills/dev-flow/SKILL.md:~110, Stage protocol; repeated in references/stage-graph.md "Urgent placement") also fires for `S!`. There `--to code-review` exits 3 with qc-gate in legal_next, and the text then tells the agent "finish-flow runs the code-review after finish". §2.7 says that for XS/S urgency is a mark only and no code-review exists. The walk itself stays legal (exit 3 writes nothing, qc-gate is taken), so the only effect is a possibly spurious post-finish review attempt, depending on finish-flow (K7). Scoping the row to M/L/XL is a guidance edit that needs a new eval arm, so it is deferred.
🔵 [k6-urgent-db-migration-bump] CUT/FOLLOW-UP At skills/dev-flow/SKILL.md:~405 (§ Urgent), "A DB migration ⇒ STOP: `session-mode.js set --size L`" replaces the old "re-route to L". An upward set mid-walk resumes via `next` from the current stage, so L's intent/plan/plan-review are not owed retroactively, and a migration hotfix found after `implement` gets code-review+qc but no plan. This matches the §2.7 E1 rule ("earlier nodes are not retroactively required"), so it is consistent with the frozen plan. Noted as a possible future gate; it is not a defect.
